nf-core is a community built around nextflow, where people build nextflow pipelines on different bioinformatics data. 

## why use nf-core?
When we want to analyse data, we can be pretty sure that a pipeline for that type of data probably already exists. So we can save time and effort by using an already validated pipeline, built and maintained by an expert. We also get all the benefits of nextflow, like reproducibility and portability. 

## setup
So now all we have to do is to create a pixi environment containing nextflow and nf-core:
```bash
pixi init nextflow_test -c conda-forge -c bioconda
cd nextflow_test
pixi add nextflow nf-core
```

## test run
In this example, we will use the Sarek pipeline:
```bash
pixi run nextflow run nf-core/sarek -profile test --outdir sarek_test -c hpc2n.config
```
hpc2n.config is a configuration file that we need to run this pipeline on our cluster!

## running nf-core pipeline on real data!
We first made a samplesheet with the samples we wanted to analyse. Then we added it to the form on the nf-core launcher and ran it as a batch job:
```bash
pixi run nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq -r 3.26.0 -params-file nf-params.json -c hpc2n.config
```
